title: Launch Connector: Sprint Cadence, Cross-Train Sync and Contingency Orchestra
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Goal: Define and operationalize a lightweight "connector" cadence that harmonizes runtime, console, and API release trains for April 2026 launches. The connector cadence creates a predictable windowing pattern, guardrails for capacity and rollback, and a contingency orchestra so teams can opt into coordinated cutovers with minimal manual coordination. This ticket captures the PM plan, acceptance criteria, owners, required engineering/design tasks, and cross-team sign-offs.
acceptance_criteria: A cadence playbook that specifies weekly windows and an explicit preflight checklist is published to Confluence and linked from the Console launch UI.
Deployment orchestration templates (k8s job + runbook automation) exist for the two contingency lanes: warm-fallback and cold-fallback.
Cross-train ownership matrix is approved by runtime, console, and API leads and mapped to on-call rotations for the launch week.
Automated canary/health checks and a smoke dashboard are deployed; SLO regressions trigger rollback policy specified in the playbook.
Runbook automation can initiate rollback or capacity re-route within 5 minutes of a critical signal during the launch window.
tasks: PM: finalize cadence windows and blackout constraints (PM-178234-1).
ENG: add cutover signal hooks in runtime routing service and expose metrics (ENG-21045).
ENG: create automation playbook for warm-fallback lane (ENG-21092).
DES: design a lightweight Console banner and launch card for showing cutover state (DES-8763).
SRE: author the smoke dashboard and SLO regression alerts (ENG-21211).
PM: coordinate stakeholder sign-off and publish Confluence playbook (PM-178234-2).
QA: create a minimal e2e harness to shadow traffic during the canary window (ENG-21350).
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting held with runtime, console, API, SRE. Initial concerns: capacity reservation for Dedicated customers during canary. Action: quantify 95th percentile token throughput by 2026-02-20.
2026-02-24: Runtime team proposed a warm-fallback lane that keeps a pinned model variant hot for 30 minutes post-cutover. ENG follow-up to estimate GPU costs by 2026-03-02.
2026-03-02: SRE delivered draft smoke dashboard and alert thresholds. PM requested a low-latency health check that verifies KV cache priming; engineering to prototype in 2 sprints.
2026-03-06: Design preview approved for Console launch card. Minor copy edits requested to emphasize rollback triggers and contact channels.
2026-03-09: Cross-train ownership matrix circulated; runtime lead (Mei Chen) and API lead (Rahul Desai) approved. Next: schedule dry-run for April 1st window.
risks: Dedicated capacity spikes could cause cost overrun during warm-fallback; need reservation budget or rollback cost cap.
Insufficient KV cache priming will inflate latency for early traffic, increasing user-visible failures.
Cross-team scheduling conflicts during April windows could force a partial roll that leaves some surfaces degraded.
Automation gaps in rollback could result in manual, time-consuming cutovers.
